cards.back: Writing a number as a product of prime numbers only. Example: 12 = 2 × 2 × 3.
cards.say: What is prime factorisation? Writing a number as a product of prime numbers only. Example: twelve equals two times two times three.
Prime factors of twelve. two times two times three
Prime factors of thirty six. two times two times three times three
Prime factors of forty five. three times three times five
Prime factors of forty eight. two times two times two times two times three
Prime factors of sixty. two times two times three times five
Prime factors of seventy two. two times two times two times three times three
Prime factors of eighty four. two times two times three times seven
Prime factors of one hundred. two times two times five times five

cards.front: How many primes are less than 20?
cards.say: How many primes are less than twenty? eight: two, three, five, seven, eleven, thirteen, seventeen, nineteen.
Primes between thirty and fifty. thirty one, thirty seven, forty one, forty three, forty seven

cards.back: 97. It is the only prime between 90 and 100.
cards.say: Which prime is between ninety and one hundred? ninety seven. It is the only prime between ninety and one hundred.

cards.back: Two primes that differ by 2. Examples: 11 and 13, 17 and 19.
cards.say: Twin primes. Two primes that differ by two. Examples: eleven and thirteen, seventeen and nineteen.

cards.back: The highest common factor: the biggest number that divides exactly into two or more numbers.
cards.say: What is the HCF? The highest common factor: the biggest number that divides exactly into two or more numbers.

cards.back: The lowest common multiple: the smallest number that is a multiple of two or more numbers.
cards.say: What is the LCM? The lowest common multiple: the smallest number that is a multiple of two or more numbers.

cards.back: 12. Factors of 24 and 36 both include 12, and nothing bigger.
cards.say: HCF of twenty four and thirty six. twelve. Factors of twenty four and thirty six both include twelve, and nothing bigger.
HCF of eighteen and twenty seven. nine
HCF of sixteen and forty. eight
LCM of six and eight. twenty four. Multiples of six: six, twelve, eighteen, twenty four. Multiples of eight: eight, sixteen, twenty four.
LCM of nine and twelve. thirty six
LCM of four and ten. twenty

cards.back: 35. They share no factor except 1, so multiply: 5 × 7 = 35.
cards.say: Lowest common multiple of five and seven. Thirty five. They share no factor except one, so multiply them.

cards.front: One bus comes every 6 minutes and another every 8 minutes. If they leave together now, when do they next leave together?
cards.back: After 24 minutes. The LCM of 6 and 8 is 24.
cards.say: One bus comes every six minutes and another every eight minutes. If they leave together now, when do they next leave together? After twenty four minutes. The LCM of six and eight is twenty four.

cards.back: No. A prime has exactly two factors, and 1 has only one.
cards.say: Is one a prime number? No. A prime has exactly two factors, and one has only one.
